From the Editor

There’s a person on the other side of every failure.

There are enough success stories. SECOND TAKE asks leaders what they chose the second time — after the first take went wrong — and records the doubt behind the numbers in their own words.

Short ReadsJust the decision, for busy days

ST.001Ryo Saeki

The morning after he decided to close the company, he couldn’t say a word

  1. Two months of cash left, and the CEO had decided to close.
  2. Faced with a rescue plan his team wrote overnight, he held back the announcement.
  3. He chose to keep the customers, not the size of the company.
Read the brief→

ST.002Nao Kuroda

She knew it would fail. It still took her a year to stop

  1. Revenue was growing, but few customers stayed past three months.
  2. Encouraging messages led her to move the exit line three times.
  3. She made the rule impossible to change alone — and closed the business.
Read the brief→

ST.003Keisuke Mori

He left to protect it: 143 days to walk away from the company he founded

  1. Every decision ran through the founder, and the organization slowed down.
  2. Before choosing a successor, he gave up his own role.
  3. Over 143 days he handed over authority and stepped outside.
Read the brief→
